new.s:
With reference to cybercrime in NCRB Crime in India 2024, consider the following statements:
1. Cybercrime cases crossed 1 lakh for the first time.
2. Fraud accounted for about 72.6% of cybercrime cases.
3. Sexual exploitation accounted for more than half of cybercrime cases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: cybercrime reached 1,01,928 cases in 2024, the first time above 1 lakh, and 72.6% was fraud. Statement 3 is wrong because sexual exploitation was only 3.1% (3,190 cases). So options with statement 3 fail.
new.tq: Cybercrime 2024: 1,01,928 (first time > 1 lakh); 72.6% fraud, 3.1% sexual exploitation.

new.s: Which provision of the Constitution of India prohibits traffic in human beings?
new.x: Article 23(1) prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour. Article 21A is the right to education, Article 24 bars child labour in hazardous employment, and Article 39(f) is a Directive Principle on protecting children from exploitation.

new.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 because:
o: It got fewer votes in favour than against
It got 298 votes in favour against 230, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority
The Rajya Sabha had rejected it first
It needed ratification by half the States, which was refused
new.x: It won a simple majority (298 for, 230 against, of 528 present and voting) but fell short of the 352 votes needed for the special majority under Article 368. It was not defeated on a simple vote, the Rajya Sabha did not vote first, and State ratification was not the reason.

new.s: Which one of the following statements about the National Commission for Women is correct?
o: It is a constitutional body set up under Article 338
It is a statutory body set up in 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990
It was created by an executive resolution in 2001
It is a statutory body under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
new.x: The NCW was set up in 1992 as a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990. It reviews safeguards, recommends measures and handles grievances. It is not a constitutional body (Article 338 is the SC Commission), not an executive creation, and not set up under the DV Act.
